title: Elide legacy IO buffering and introduce adaptive KV snapshotting
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: We have observed recurring tail-latency regressions caused by a legacy IO buffering layer that serializes small KV writes and forces synchronous fsyncs during cache compaction. This ticket removes the old io-buffering adapter, replaces it with an async coalescer, and implements an adaptive KV snapshotting strategy that reduces write amplification during heavy continuous-batching workloads. Goal: reduce p99 token latency under heavy multiplexing by 15-25% and reduce compaction-related CPU spikes.
background: During the 2025 Q4 incidents we traced several sustained p99 spikes to the path where compacted KV metadata was flushed synchronously by the legacy io adapter. The adapter was originally added for Windows consistency and backwards compatibility with the on-disk journal; over time the runtime accumulated exceptions and ad-hoc patches to work around it. Upgrading the underlying storage dependency (rocksdb -> rocksdb-optimized fork) exposed more of the synchronous behavior. This refactor pairs a lightweight async coalescer with a tunable snapshot scheduler that observes batch size and active in-flight sessions.
technical_approach: Audit current io-buffering adapter and list all callsites that rely on sync fsync semantics
Remove legacy adapter and add AsyncWriteCoalescer component with a bounded delay window (default 8ms) and max coalesced payload
Introduce AdaptiveKVSnapshotter that monitors batch depth, average seq len, and kv-write rate to decide between incremental snapshot vs full checkpoint
Upgrade storage dependency to rocksdb-opt@2.1.0 (requires symbols change) and add compatibility shim for table-format detection
Add integration harness that replays production batch traces (stored in s3) to validate correctness and measure latency impact
Add unit/e2e tests for crash-consistency by simulating mid-snapshot restarts and verifying KV recovery
Rollout behind runtime feature-flag and canary 2% traffic -> 10% -> 50% with automatic rollback on error-rate regressions
acceptance_criteria: Legacy io-buffering adapter removed from runtime tree and no longer built by default
p99 token latency in sustained 5000 qps continuous-batching synthetic load is reduced by >=15% compared to baseline
KV compaction-related CPU spikes reduced (95th percentile CPU per pod down by >=10%)
No correctness regressions: snapshot recovery passes the replay harness and CI fuzzing
Ship with feature flag and automated canary rollout plan documented in the PR and runbook
migration_plan: Step 1: Merge AsyncWriteCoalescer behind feature-flag in runtime main branch (unit tests + e2e harness)
Step 2: Run storage upgrade tests on staging (rocksdb-opt@2.1.0) and confirm table-format compatibility
Step 3: Enable feature-flag for internal canary fleet (2%) and monitor for 48h
Step 4: Expand canary to customer-visible dedicated clusters (10%) with heightened telemetry
Step 5: Gradual global rollout with health gates and automatic rollback on latency/regression signals
Step 6: Once stable, flip default and schedule small cleanup PR to remove shim code and adapter stubs
monitoring_and_rollout: Dashboard: runtime/kv/snapshotting (graphs: p50/p95/p99 token latency, kv_write_rate, coalesce_delay_histogram)
Alert: if p99 increases >10% vs baseline for 30m during canary -> pause rollout
Saga timers to detect hung coalescer threads (metric: coalescer_pending_batches > 5 for 1m)
Log correlation IDs added to snapshot start/finish events for tracing in Jaeger
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: coalescer delay may increase tail latency for small single-token requests. Mitigation: bounded delay and fast-path for single-inflight-session low-latency class
Risk: storage upgrade incompatibility. Mitigation: compatibility shim + table-format detection + offline migration job if needed
Risk: snapshotting bug could cause data loss. Mitigation: extensive replay harness, crash-consistency tests, and staged rollout
Risk: increased memory pressure when coalescing large payloads. Mitigation: bounded coalesce size and backpressure into batch admission controller
